prompt:
Write the appraiser's remarks (about 80 words) on a body shop repair estimate after a hit while turning left. Describe the damage seen on the vehicle and the repair plan. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1038; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The bills show no repeated charges.
- The repair labor hours are a little high for this damage.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
text: The rear quarter panel and bumper cover on the left side show crushed metal, a cracked lamp housing and scuffing that line up with a vehicle striking the side while turning left. The pattern of contact fits the account given and no older damage has come to light. The shop plans to replace the bumper cover, straighten the quarter panel, refinish both areas and fit a new lamp assembly. Parts and paint figures look reasonable on the invoices, which show no duplicated charges. The labor hours appear somewhat high for this scope of work and should be reviewed against standard repair times before approval.
